Un investigador conocido por desenmascarar a los peces gordos del ecosistema Ransomware GangExposed logro dar con la verdadera identidad del administrador de la padilla de Ransowmare Qilin.

 Se trata de un hombre ruso de 36 años llamado Alexey Mikhailovich Yakovtsev el cual operaba en distintos foros de piratas informáticos con el nick Rjun.

En el articulo de la investigación se puede ver como logro obtener información valiosa de los datos de filtración de BreachForums, obteniendo su correo electrónico personal y su IP (Rusia)

ARTICULO INVESTIGACION:
https://justpaste.it/iosba

On affected Alpine Linux servers, SSH rejects a wrong password but can accept ANY password between 257 and 1,024 bytes for an account with no password set.

One long string is enough. No brute force needed.

Not every Alpine Linux server is vulnerable.

The bypass requires:
• SSH password logins enabled
• Password checks without PAM
• An account with no password set
• Another account with a compatible password hash

Key-only accounts can be exposed too.


It gets worse on certain Alpine cloud images.

The alpine user has passwordless doas access. If the SSH bypass conditions are met, an attacker can log in as alpine and become root.

OpenSSH and Alpine have released fixes.

Can't update yet? Set PasswordAuthentication no and restart sshd.

‼️ BREAKING: OpenSSH has rushed out a fix for a critical flaw that lets attackers log into some Linux servers without the right password.

The team learned of the bug a day earlier. OpenSSH's Damien Miller says long embargoes now mostly help attackers, because AI agents rediscover bugs, sometimes within hours.

It hits Linux systems on the musl C library with PAM off, such as Alpine Linux. Miller told admins to disable password logins or SSH itself "IMMEDIATELY".

Version 10.6p2 works around it. Systems on glibc or PAM are not affected, and Miller says the root cause sits outside OpenSSH.
